item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"Treat d1o5dt2 as an incomplete observation of the b.1.2.1 fibronectin type III family, not automatically as a naturally shorter or highly divergent domain. Align only its resolved, homologous FNIII core to d1uc6a1; handle absent termini or unresolved segments as missing coverage rather than evolutionary deletions, and report coverage alongside sequence/structural similarity. Prefer the more complete d1uc6a1 as the general family representative or modeling template. Retain d1o5dt2 only when it contributes distinct, well-covered sequence/structural variation, with its fragment status explicit; it should not alone define domain boundaries, profile lengths, or family-wide features. Its inclusion may broaden observed local variation, but missing regions must not be counted as family diversity or evidence of a new architecture. Shared SCOPe family assignment supports relatively close homology, yet does not by itself justify transferring ligand binding, biological function, or full-domain structural features. Interpretation should ideally be checked against SCOPe domain boundaries and PDB construct/SEQRES-versus-coordinate coverage to distinguish engineered truncation, disorder, and unresolved residues.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
